problems.title: Invent yourself
problems.statement: It is more difficult to bend a paper sheet, if it is folded “accordion style” or rolled into a tube. Using a single A4 sheet and a small amount of glue, if required, construct a bridge spanning a gap of 280 mm. Introduce parameters to describe the strength of your bridge, and optimise some or all of them.

solution.incompleteReason: IYPT publishes no official solutions; the problems are open research tasks.

problems.title: Elastic space
problems.statement: The dynamics and apparent interactions of massive balls rolling on a stretched horizontal membrane are often used to illustrate gravitation. Investigate the system further. Is it possible to define and measure the apparent “gravitational constant” in such a “world”?

solution.incompleteReason: IYPT publishes no official solutions; the problems are open research tasks.

problems.title: Bouncing ball
problems.statement: If you hold a Ping-Pong ball above the ground and release it, it bounces. The nature of the collision changes if the ball contains liquid. Investigate how the nature of the collision depends on the amount of liquid inside the ball and other relevant parameters.

solution.incompleteReason: IYPT publishes no official solutions; the problems are open research tasks.

problems.title: Soliton
problems.statement: A chain of similar pendula is mounted equidistantly along a horizontal axis, with adjacent pendula being connected with light strings. Each pendulum can rotate about the axis but can not move sideways (see figure). Investigate the propagation of a deflection along such a chain. What is the speed for a solitary wave, when each pendulum undergoes an entire 360º revolution?

figures.alt: Hand-drawn sketch of a row of pendula hanging from a horizontal axis and joined by strings; along the chain the pendula swing through a full turn, forming a travelling twist. An arrow labelled c shows the propagation direction, and a curved arrow labelled ω marks the rotation at the end of the chain.

solution.incompleteReason: IYPT publishes no official solutions; the problems are open research tasks.

problems.title: Levitation
problems.statement: A light ball (e.g. a Ping-Pong ball) can be supported on an upward airstream. The airstream can be tilted yet still support the ball. Investigate the effect and optimise the system to produce the maximum angle of tilt that results in a stable ball position.

problems.title: Coloured plastic
problems.statement: In bright light, a transparent plastic object (e.g. a blank CD case) can sometimes shine in various colours (see figure). Study and explain the phenomenon. Ascertain if one also sees the colours when various light sources are used.

figures.alt: Photograph of a transparent plastic CD case lying at an angle in bright light, showing rainbow-coloured interference fringes across its surface.

problems.title: Hearing light
problems.statement: Coat one half of the inside of a jar with a layer of soot and drill a hole in its cover (see figure). When light from a light bulb connected to AC hits the jar’s black wall, a distinct sound can be heard. Explain and investigate the phenomenon.

figures.alt: Drawing of a light bulb shining yellow rays onto a transparent jar lying on its side; the lower half of the jar's inside is dark (soot-coated) and the blue cover at the right end has a small hole in its centre.

problems.title: Jet and film
problems.statement: A thin liquid jet impacts on a soap film (see figure). Depending on relevant parameters, the jet can either penetrate through the film or merge with it, producing interesting shapes. Explain and investigate this interaction and the resulting shapes.

figures.alt: Photograph of a thin liquid jet striking a soap film stretched on a white wire frame, with the jet bending and spreading along the film.

problems.title: Helmholtz carousel
problems.statement: Attach Christmas tree balls on a low friction mounting (carousel) such that the hole in each ball points in a tangential direction. If you expose this arrangement to sound of a suitable frequency and intensity, the carousel starts to rotate. Explain this phenomenon and investigate the parameters that result in the maximum rotation speed of the carousel.
